articles.title: Idaho's closed horse track reopens as $42m public park with restored wetlands

articles.title: Who is IPS officer Aditya Kumar? Fake Chief Justice case, CAT ruling, suspension and DIG promotion explained
articles.summary: Bihar IPS officer Aditya Kumar faces disciplinary proceedings over an alleged conspiracy to impersonate a former Patna High Court Chief Justice. The CAT has refused to quash the inquiry, while a separate departmental case against him has been closed.

articles.title: UK on emergency? PM Andy Burnham urges citizens to store 3 days of food, water and cash at home; here's what's happening
articles.summary: The UK government has launched the ‘Be Ready campaign and urged people to store essential items such as food, water, cash and more at home for up to three days. Here’s why it is important amid wildfires, storm, cybersecurity threats and more in the nation.

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi's Nov 1 INDIA bloc rally: Delhi's CTI cites  ₹25K cr Dhanteras business, seeks delay— What letter to MP said
articles.summary: Delhi’s Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has urged Rahul Gandhi to postpone the Congress rally planned for November 1 at Ramlila Maidan until after November 10, citing potential disruption to festive-season business and traffic near major markets and railway stations.

articles.title: 4 Philippine Air Force pilots killed as 2 training aircraft collide midair: Report
articles.summary: The two SF-260 aircraft collided while flying at a low altitude during a training flight on Friday afternoon before crashing at Fernando Air Base in Lipa city, located in the coastal province of Batangas

articles.title: Iran claims control of Strait of Hormuz, says 2 oil tankers hit mines, warns US warships against Persian Gulf entry
articles.summary: Iran claims control over the Strait of Hormuz and says two oil supertankers carrying over 4.5 million barrels struck naval mines. The claims remain unverified as Tehran warns US warships against entering the Persian Gulf amid fears of a US strike.

articles.title: Noida Sector 125 fire: Blaze at hotel spreads to nearby eateries, firefighting ops underway | Video
articles.summary: A fire at Krishna Food Point in Sector 125 on Saturday spread to nearby eateries, causing panic. Firefighters deployed four vehicles and brought the blaze under control with police assistance. No casualties were reported.

articles.title: Fodder scam case: CBI nabs Satyendra Kumar, accused on the run for 25 years from Lucknow station; all you need to know
articles.summary: The CBI arrested fodder scam accused Satyendra Kumar at Lucknow railway station after 25 years on the run. Traced to Nepal before returning to India, he is being brought to Ranchi on transit remand to face court proceedings.

articles.title: ‘838’ number plate, pool of blood, screams: Chilling video captures daylight murder
articles.summary: In a shocking act of violence in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, bystanders witnessed a murder as Devesh Dixit was pursued and collided with a vehicle. His friend-turned-assailant, Pawan Parashar, went on to deliver a fatal blow using a stick and iron rod. The police arrived shortly after, and Parashar voluntarily surrendered later at the station. Investigations continue to reveal the motive behind this brutal attack.

articles.title: Burnt body of Class 12 student found behind guard room at Delhi school
articles.summary: An 18-year-old girl was discovered burnt behind the guard room of a school in Krishna Nagar. Police received a call regarding the fire incident and promptly arrived at the scene. They conducted preliminary proceedings and collected materials from the spot, including the victim's school bag. A crime team thoroughly inspected the location to gather evidence for the ongoing investigation.

When Sonia met Rajiv: Congress leader narrates her 1st meeting with husband in X debut
articles.summary: Sonia Gandhi officially joined the social media platform X to share personal memories and insights. In her first post, she introduced her upcoming memoir titled Belonging: A Journey of Love. The memoir recounts her life experiences, including her first meeting with Rajiv Gandhi in Cambridge. Scheduled for release on November 10, the book details her journey through love and loss.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos’s parents bet $245,573 on Amazon; their early stake worth billions today

Kentucky court rejects bid to use neighbour's driveway after land split
articles.summary: In a Kentucky court case, Charlie E. Stearns and Kathy Stearns faced a setback in their property dispute against neighbors John and Betty Warinner. The Stearnses asserted that their long-term use of a pathway should grant them an implied easement. However, the jury found alternative access routes viable, leading to the dismissal of their claim, a verdict affirmed by the appeals court, confirming that historical usage doesn’t automatically legitimize easements.

articles.title: Watch: Two Philippine air force trainer aircraft collide mid-air; 4 pilots killed
Tilak Varma breaks world record during India vs New Zealand 2nd T20I
articles.summary: Tilak Varma achieved a historic milestone by taking the most catches in T20 Internationals during 2026. His remarkable performance included two catches in the second T20I against New Zealand. Varma surpassed the previous record held by Danilson Hawoe with a total of 26 catches this year. India won the toss and opted to bowl, making two changes to their playing XI.

articles.title: Megan Thee Stallion-backed project delivers over 2,200 care packs to Black girls
articles.summary: In January 2024, 12-year-old Mila Henry founded MH Boxes, aiming to support Black girls facing mental health challenges. With a $550 grant from the #BlackGirlJoyChallenge, she crafted care packages containing essential self-care items. To date, the initiative has successfully distributed over 3,300 boxes nationwide, striving to break the stigma surrounding mental health in the Black community.

articles.title: New York court revives privacy claim over cameras filming family's backyard
articles.summary: A couple in New York found themselves entangled in a complex property disagreement with their neighbors regarding a disputed land boundary tied to a chain-link fence. This conflict escalated, resulting in claims of trespassing and invasion of privacy due to surveillance cameras. Although the court struggled to rule on the boundary dispute, it has permitted the couple's privacy claims to advance for further scrutiny.

articles.title: As Tesla promotes product Musk predicted 80% of value will come from, costs jump
articles.summary: Elon Musk has announced the start of production for Tesla's humanoid robot, named Optimus, in Fremont, California. The production phase is still in its early stages and might experience challenges. Despite a decline in revenue from Tesla's solar and energy storage business, there is positive growth in its services sector. Musk estimates the company could manufacture 20,000 robots per week by the end of 2027.

articles.title: Denied library entry as boy, he helped open one; graduates rose from 4 to 30
articles.summary: Faced with caste discrimination when trying to access a library, V Selvakumar took matters into his own hands by starting a project to create one in Semmadu village. The result? A remarkable leap in educational achievement, with graduates rising from four to thirty. The local community, including youth and officials, rallied to sustain the library, emphasizing the transformative power of equitable educational access.

articles.title: 'Trump will take his dream to his grave': Iran says won't allow US warships in Hormuz
articles.summary: Iran has expressed its determination to prevent US military presence in the Persian Gulf amid escalating tensions. US Ambassador to Turkiye Tom Barrack mentioned the potential for a US strike on Iran this weekend. Despite threats, Barrack stated that President Trump continues to seek a diplomatic agreement. Trump emphasised that further military action remains a possibility if negotiations do not progress.

articles.title: How Jeffrey Epstein became Houthis' new weapon against Saudi Arabia
Did Van Gogh’s ‘Starry Night’ depict real sky from July 1889? Scientists think so
articles.summary: In a groundbreaking study, South Korean researchers have pinpointed July 22, 1889, as a possible date for the celestial scene depicted in The Starry Night. This new timeline disputes the widely accepted June 1889 date. The study notes that the alignment of stars aligns with observations from that evening, bolstered by van Gogh's letters that reference weather conditions, suggesting the artist's keen attention to his surroundings.

articles.title: 'Four years, I never chased this jersey': Bhuvneshwar Kumar on India comeback
articles.summary: Bhuvneshwar Kumar credited patience, preparation and a no-expectations mindset for helping him return to international cricket after four years. The 36-year-old said the IPL and domestic cricket kept him sharp while improving his maturity. He also discussed modern T20 challenges, stressing that bowlers need smart strategies. India's strong start against New Zealand, he added, could boost confidence throughout the tour.

articles.title: ‘Noise protest’ rocks Manipur valley districts, police fire tear gas
articles.summary: In a powerful display of unity, thousands of demonstrators took to the streets in various valley districts of Manipur, articulating their concerns over the escalating crisis. Using traditional means of noise-making, they called for urgent government intervention. Key demands included the establishment of the National Register of Citizens and an improved response to ethnic tensions, showcasing a strong public insistence for accountability and resolution.

articles.title: 13k Pilibhit voter details changed, UP CEO calls it a ‘deliberate crime’
articles.summary: In a significant turn of events, an FIR has been filed against two SDMs and a voter registration operator due to allegations of fraudulent voter roll modifications. This manipulation has impacted more than 13,150 voters in the Pilibhit assembly constituency. The Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer emphasized the intentional nature of this act, calling it a crime rather than negligence.

articles.title: IPL 2027: Steffan Jones joins Mumbai Indians as bowling consultant
articles.summary: Mumbai Indians (MI) have roped in former Rajasthan Royals high-performance coach Steffan Jones as a bowling consultant for their development squad. Jones will work with MI's development squad alongside director of performance Zubin Bharucha, with the duo tasked with helping Indian players improve their skillsets.

articles.title: Australian umpire's Ranji sojourn: Planes overhead at Palam, BKC's red soil pitch
articles.summary: Australian umpire Ben Treloar is experiencing Indian domestic cricket for the first time as part of the BCCI-Cricket Australia exchange programme. From aeroplanes flying overhead at Delhi's Palam ground to Mumbai's red-soil pitch at BKC, the 44-year-old shares his impressions of Indian first-class cricket, the warmth of its people and his growing love for local cuisine, including garlic naan and vada pav.

articles.title: IND vs NZ: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in playing XI, but there's a twist
articles.summary: India captain Shreyas Iyer won the toss and elected to bowl first against New Zealand in the second T20. The team made two changes, with 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi replacing Ishan Kishan and Prince Yadav coming in for Mayank Yadav. Iyer emphasized the importance of maintaining their aggressive approach while addressing fielding improvements. New Zealand also made a change, bringing in Jacob Duffy for Adam Milne.

articles.title: North Korea's Kim Jong-un makes surprise visit to China via newly opened bridge
Husband’s illicit relationship by itself is not cruelty: Madras high court
articles.summary: Madras high court ruled that a husband's illicit relationship is not sufficient for cruelty under Section 498A. This ruling came from a case involving a woman who committed suicide with her child. The court noted that more evidence is required to establish cruelty beyond mere allegations of an affair. The trial court had acquitted the husband due to insufficient evidence linking him to dowry harassment.

articles.title: From fuel price hikes to cost-of-living concerns, US consumer sentiment nears record low
articles.summary: US consumer sentiment has declined slightly as rising prices related to the Middle East conflict affect households' financial views. The Consumer Sentiment Index fell marginally to 48.0 in October, approaching a record low. Independents reported significantly weaker sentiment while Democrats and Republicans showed improvements. Inflation expectations rose, suggesting concerns about future price increases among consumers. The Federal Reserve is expected to maintain current interest rates during their upcoming meeting.

articles.title: 'Rs 10k cr at risk': Traders' body urges Rahul to defer Delhi rally amid Diwali season
India script history with best-ever finish and record 114 medals at Asian Para Games
articles.summary: India concluded the Asian Para Games 2026 with an extraordinary display of talent, amassing a total of 114 medals, consisting of 30 gold, 35 silver, and 49 bronze. This achievement surpasses their previous record from 2022 edition, securing a commendable fourth place overall. The rise of India's para-athletes on the continental stage was evident, even as China led with an impressive 217 gold medals.

The accused was reportedly under the influence of alcohol when he attacked the doctor. Medical officers in Wardha district protested by boycotting work, highlighting safety concerns for healthcare personnel. Subsequently, police registered a case against the accused based on the medical officer's complaint.

articles.title: As foam builds up in Yamuna, questions raised over how work was allotted
articles.summary: A defoaming operation is set to begin in Yamuna near Kalindi Kunj, with equipment already in place. The Aam Aadmi Party has raised concerns about the tender allocation process favoring a specific contractor. Allegations state that the contractor set up equipment before the bids were officially opened. Delhi Jal Board representatives clarify that they have conducted defoaming campaigns annually since 2022.

11-year-old Indian-origin prodigy Bodhana breaks Polgar's 38-yo record
articles.summary: Eleven-year-old British chess prodigy Bodhana Sivanandan has become the youngest female player to qualify for the International Master title, breaking Judit Polgar’s 38-year-old record. The English Chess Federation praised her as a “generational talent.” Already the youngest Woman Grandmaster qualifier, Bodhana has achieved several historic milestones and is now aiming to become a Grandmaster, chess’s highest title.

articles.title: Watch: Paris shops increase security, board up windows, as France braces for protests
articles.summary: Shopkeepers in Paris are taking measures to secure their businesses against possible renewed protests and violence. Authorities are increasing police presence, with around 70,000 officers deployed this weekend across France. Demonstrations are planned in several cities, amidst ongoing political tensions leading to protests against rising living costs. While some support the protests, others condemn the associated looting and vandalism.

articles.title: Mumbai Indians appoint Kieron Pollard as head coach ahead of IPL 2027
articles.summary: Kieron Pollard has been named the head coach of Mumbai Indians ahead of the IPL 2027 season. He takes over the position from Mahela Jayawardene, who has stepped down. Pollard expressed his gratitude for the opportunity and emphasised his connection to the team. The franchise is hopeful that Pollard will help restore their winning form. Mumbai Indians aims to build on their past successes and inspire their fans.

18-year-old Anahat's historic run at Silicon Valley Open comes to an end
articles.summary: India’s Anahat Singh exited the Silicon Valley Open after losing 3-1 to Malaysia’s Sivasangari Subramaniam despite winning the opening game. Sivasangari praised the 18-year-old’s talent and potential after staging a comeback. Anahat had earlier defeated world No. 14 Salma Hany to become the first Indian woman since 2019 to reach a PSA Tour Gold-level semifinal.

articles.title: 'Now is the time': Rubio warns Cuba next after Iran, asks Cubans to join hands
articles.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called on Cubans to collaborate with intelligence agencies for positive change. He criticized the Cuban regime for corruption and unmet promises, suggesting this moment is crucial for action. The CIA later released a recruitment video encouraging Cubans to provide information discreetly. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump mentioned potential military actions nearby, heightening tensions over the situation.

articles.title: Over 100 detained as SIR protests continue in Delhi
articles.summary: Hundreds of protesters including students and farmers gathered in Delhi to demand the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. They criticized the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls for resulting in unfair voter deletions. Many demonstrators were detained by police as tensions escalated during the protest. Demonstrations have been organized in 88 cities across 18 states involving numerous organizations.

articles.title: Delhi HC junks Neha Bora plea against peace bond notice
articles.summary: The Delhi high court has denied AISA president Neha Bora's request to challenge a peace bond notice, which was raised amid concerns of potential peace disruption in a busy commercial district. The court determined that the special executive magistrate had enough evidence to issue the notice against Bora, who is facing several FIRs from the Delhi Police regarding public order violations.

articles.title: Diljit Dosanjh's Delhi gig gets police nod amid fresh threats
articles.summary: With security concerns arising, the Delhi Police initially refused to grant permission for Diljit Dosanjh's upcoming concert. Following constructive discussions with the organisers, improved safety protocols were established, including the addition of 1,500 personnel for crowd management. Attendees will be updated about transportation options in collaboration with cab providers. The concert is officially rescheduled for October 30 at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium.

articles.title: Haryana power cut: Homes in dark for hours, residents block roads
articles.summary: A two-day power strike in Haryana caused significant disruptions across Gurgaon and surrounding areas. Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini assured employees that no private power distribution licenses would be permitted. Outages led to water supply disruptions and industrial production halts, impacting many residents and businesses. Appeals were made by industry bodies for urgent government intervention to restore power.

articles.title: ITBP Raising Day: PM Modi praises ‘Himveers’ as India-China border remains in focus
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and other leaders extended their greetings to ITBP personnel on the occasion. They praised the courage and sacrifices made by the force in protecting India's borders. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh highlighted the contributions of ITBP towards internal security and border safeguarding. Meanwhile, the Indian Army and Home Minister Amit Shah also conveyed their regards.

articles.title: 15-year-old girl sexually assaulted in Telangana; 7 arrested
articles.summary: Seven individuals, including three minors, were arrested in Siddipet district for allegedly assaulting a 15-year-old girl. The incident occurred on Dasara when the victim's parents were away for agricultural work. The accused reportedly took the girl to a neighboring village and returned her the following morning. The victim identified the perpetrators, leading her father to file a police complaint.

The change comes as trade tensions and rising costs affect border-state economies and shape a close Maine Senate race.

articles.title: FBI detains gangster Himanshu Bhau, India may get custody soon
articles.summary: Himanshu Bhau, a notorious gangster from north India, was recently captured by the FBI in Las Vegas. He has been wanted for a series of violent offenses, including multiple murders and extortion schemes that have plagued Delhi and Haryana. After escaping juvenile detention in 2020, he maintained his criminal operations through illegal networks.

articles.title: Israel launches ‘limited counterterrorism’ op after 2 IDF troops killed in West Bank
articles.summary: In a post on X, the IDF said, "In response to the shooting attack in which 2 IDF soldiers fell, and several others were wounded, the IDF along with other security forces launched a targeted & limited counterterrorism operation in the Hebron area, from which the terrorists had emerged." The military said residents in areas where its forces are operating would be allowed to leave through three designated exit points.

Watch: Giant waves crash into Taiwan as Typhoon Champi leaves over 500 injured; 1 dead
articles.summary: Typhoon Champi made landfall in Taiwan, resulting in one casualty and more than 500 injuries reported. The storm brought heavy rain and strong winds, leading to widespread power outages affecting over 167,000 homes. Over 240 flights were canceled due to severe weather conditions impacting transport services. Schools and offices were closed for an extended period as a precautionary measure against the storm.

articles.title: 'We have to think about posting 350 first': Rauf on need for bigger totals
articles.summary: Haris Rauf said his role alongside Shaheen Afridi and Naseem Shah is to take wickets and strengthen Pakistan’s bowling attack. He stressed teamwork, middle-over breakthroughs and the need for bigger totals as ODI cricket becomes more aggressive. Rauf is also focusing on improving his pace and fitness, while backing Saim Ayub and Fakhar Zaman to contribute runs in upcoming matches.

articles.title: Ryan Gosling and Eva Mendes bought retreat made from 200-year-old barns in 2014
articles.summary: In 2014, Ryan Gosling and Eva Mendes purchased a distinctive rustic estate in Carpinteria, California. This property, crafted by Joel Schumacher, is constructed from reclaimed wood of three 200-year-old barns. Designed for privacy and a serene connection to nature, it embodies American history, offering a tranquil retreat from Los Angeles. The couple cherishes their family life away from the spotlight, valuing their children and preserving the estate's unique features.

articles.title: Krasinski and Emily Blunt sell Brooklyn apartment for $6.5M, net $1.5M profit
articles.summary: John Krasinski and Emily Blunt have sold their nearly 1,600-square-foot apartment at The Standish in Brooklyn Heights for $6.5 million. A trust linked to the couple purchased the property for $5 million in January 2024. The off-market sale, completed in June 2026, represents a $1.5 million increase in value in just over two years.

articles.title: Dan vs Daniel: Trump admin sues to block Alaska result if GOP candidate loses race
articles.summary: The lawsuit, filed in federal court in Alaska on Thursday, argues that the state must protect the integrity of federal elections. It asks the court to block the certification of a Peltola victory if Daniel Sullivan, a candidate from the small fishing community of Petersburg, remains on the ballot. “The United States accordingly brings this lawsuit to protect the integrity of the 2026 Senate election in Alaska,” the lawsuit says.

articles.title: Video: Gunmen storm Jordan church during funeral, killing 7 and wounding 40
articles.summary: Jordan's government described the attackers as unknown assailants and said investigations were moving ahead at full speed. It did not immediately confirm whether any suspects had been arrested or killed. Footage aired by Jordanian state television showed two men appearing to carry pistols approaching the church and firing shots. A third man, apparently carrying a semi-automatic rifle, then approached and opened fire before all three ran towards the building.

articles.title: Tom Brady helped provide 750,000 meals to families in need in Tampa Bay
articles.summary: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen donated funds to provide 750,000 meals through Feeding Tampa Bay, supporting children, families and senior citizens in need. The contribution came shortly after the couple moved to Florida, where Brady began his career with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after 20 seasons with the New England Patriots. Their donation helped address food insecurity and supported local families facing financial hardship, highlighting their commitment to their new community.

articles.title: IND vs NZ 2nd T20I: Will Ishan Kishan's injury be Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's gain?

articles.title: Two critical PHP flaws trigger global alert; millions of services face cyber risk
articles.summary: PHP advised users on Oct 23 to temporarily disable its session upload progress feature until the next regular bugfix release. The warning followed an earlier advisory on Oct 21 about a related vulnerability. The latest issue affects applications only when specific session settings are changed while running and the upload progress feature remains enabled. Users who have already disabled the feature do not need to take further action.

articles.title: Cuba next? Trump hints at 'little stopover' after US warships return from Iran war
articles.summary: Trump and Rubio have both adopted a hard line towards Cuba's communist government. In May, the two renewed the possibility of US military intervention, with the threat gaining further significance after the Trump administration announced criminal charges against former Cuban leader Raúl Castro. Trump had floated a similar idea earlier this year but had not raised it publicly in recent months.

articles.title: China’s patrolling deviations disturb border: MEA on ITBP DG's face-offs remark
articles.summary: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday did not go into the specifics of the latest face-off, choosing to refer the issue to the defence ministry, but said Chinese divergence from established patrolling patterns created disturbances at the border from time to time. The official said both sides continued to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC.

articles.title: Upper layer NBFCs have to list: RBI guv on Tatas; dispels doubts on Sept order
articles.summary: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra’s comments also suggest Tata Sons is in breach of RBI rules. The consequences of continued noncompliance remain unclear. The governor declined to be drawn into the question of Noel Tata’s proposal to merge two Tata Sons subsidiaries with the holding company, a move that could help it sidestep a stock market listing.

articles.title: Cabinet Secretary didn’t act on EC’ plaint as it was unofficial: RTI
articles.summary: According to documents shared as part of an RTI response, two ECs in their separate but near-identical letters to Somanathan on July 29 objected to Garg’s conduct and an order he issued revising allocation of work among senior officers. The two ECs alleged the changes were made without prior discussion with the commission or officers concerned.

articles.title: Centre bans reuse of single-use medical devices across hospitals
articles.summary: In a letter dated Oct 16, the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) said it had come to its notice that some private and corporate hospitals were reusing single-use devices after sterilising them, including items used in cardiology, nephrology, oncology, cardiothoracic and vascular surgery (CTVS), neurosurgery and other clinical services. The DGHS said that reuse could expose patients to cross-infection, device malfunction, reduced performance and other complications.

articles.title: Need to unite against divisive forces, tackle new challenges: PM Modi
articles.summary: Inaugurating the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan, he said Swami Chinmayananda set his goals as per issues facing the country at the time and new challenges had emerged in the past few decades. “We must unite society against divisive forces. We must inspire citizens toward self-reliance, and we must connect every individual to vision of a developed India by 2047. For these objectives, we must become more proactive,” he said.

articles.title: Ukrainian soldier cuts off his own foot to survive, rescued by drone after 8 months
articles.summary: Kostiantyn Vlasenko, 49, had been stranded in a boiler room with severe injuries after a Russian drone strike. With no way to escape and little hope of being rescued, he made a desperate decision to amputate his remaining foot to survive. On October 4, a large drone lifted him into the air using a harness and carried him 15km to safety.

articles.title: Chloë Grace Moretz bought LA home at 19 for $3.4m, sold it for $5.65m
articles.summary: Chloë Grace Moretz purchased a $3.4 million home in Studio City in 2016 and hosted numerous gatherings there. After seven years, she listed the property for almost $6 million and sold it for $5.65 million. The home features multiple entertainment spaces, a separate studio, and luxurious outdoor areas. Studio City remains a popular area for high-profile buyers, including Olivia Wilde, who sold her property in December 2025.

articles.title: LA couple bought $925,000 farm, made barn a home, started cider business
articles.summary: David Bailey and Dana Tiel left their advertising careers to purchase a 16-acre farm in California. After spending $1 million, they converted a barn loft into their home. Their farm, Sierra Cider, includes a petting zoo, pumpkin patch and cider tastings. The couple faced challenges while balancing work and renovations during their transition. Despite initial doubts, the farm has become a popular destination for families and children.

articles.title: Slack co-founder bought Aspen estate for $25m, listed for $45m, sold for $30m
articles.summary: Stewart Butterfield and Jen Rubio recently finalized the sale of their Aspen estate for $30 million, right after their separation. They originally acquired the property for around $25 million in January 2021, yielding a nice profit despite initially aiming for $45 million. The estate has been purchased by David and Erika Sands, professional poker players, who now add it to their diverse real estate holdings across New York and California.

articles.title: Opposition's 'mock Parliament' to step up fight against SIR & CEC Gyanesh Kumar
articles.summary: Sources said a “mock” gathering depicting an assembly of MPs may take place in the national capital on Oct 28. The event will involve MPs and others, but is unlikely to be a large gathering, given that a massive show of strength to push for the CEC’s resignation is planned at Ramlila Maidan as a “Delhi chalo” rally.

articles.title: Arms training case: US mercenary VanDyke, 6 Ukrainians to remain abroad till Feb 24
articles.summary: VanDyke attended the court hearing Friday and sought the release of his seized personal articles. The seven accused had earlier sought six weeks to meet their families and were allowed to stay abroad till Oct 23. They were arrested on March 13 for allegedly training the insurgent-linked groups in Myanmar.

articles.title: Northwest India turned drier, south wetter over 70 years, finds IMD study
articles.summary: In northwest India, the hot semi-arid zone grew from about a quarter of the region’s area in 1951-1980 to a third in 1991-2020, while the temperate zone shrank from about a quarter to less than a fifth, meaning that an area equal to roughly 7% of the region moved into the drier zone as temperatures rose and rainfall declined, said the study.

articles.title: Brics parliamentary meet should end with joint statement: LS Speaker Om Birla
articles.summary: Talking to reporters Friday, Birla said the forum in India would work towards consensus-based dialogue on the role of Parliament in strengthening institutions, promotion of human-centred innovation in AI and digital technologies through Parliament, more representative system of global governance and role of Parliament in ensuring a sustainable and inclusive future for Brics countries.

articles.title: New norms for cars from 2029: Rear-crash tests, data recorders
articles.summary: The ministry has set mandatory timelines for automakers to comply with other Automotive Industry Standards (AIS), covering occupant protection in offset frontal and lateral collisions, protection of pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, and fitment of immobilisers. The requirements will come into effect from April 2027 onwards. In a notification, the ministry also made AIS-192 mandatory for Event Data Recorders (EDRs) installed in cars from Oct 2029.

articles.title: After Op Sindoor friction, Delhi & Baku reset ties with EAM Jaishankar's visit
articles.summary: Ties between the two countries had been held back by geopolitical reasons for a while, mainly Azerbaijan’s ties with Pakistan — as evident from its support for Islamabad after Op Sindoor last year — and India’s defence ties with Armenia. While Bayramov spoke about taking the relationship to a higher level, setting aside past differences, Jaishankar underlined the significance of trade and energy cooperation. Terrorism was also discussed.

articles.title: Study traces how an El Niño changed the pollution map
articles.summary: Coming ahead of India’s peak pollution season, the paper, titled ‘Air quality in flux: The baffling ENSO transition in India’, published in Atmospheric Pollution Research journal Thursday, found that La Niña/El Niño conditions altered atmospheric circulation, PM2.5 transport pathways and weather conditions that determine whether pollution disperses or gets trapped.

articles.title: Record growth, rising risks: What’s really driving India’s core industries? | The Hindu Editorial
articles.summary:
India’s core industrial sectors recorded a series-high growth rate of 7.9% in September, driven by strong performances in coal, electricity, steel and refinery products.

While the data points to a welcome industrial uptick, concerns remain about how sustainable the momentum will be. Much of the growth appears linked to temporary factors such as increased power demand during the heat wave and higher refining activity driven by imported oil.

With global crude prices rising, foreign exchange pressures mounting and infrastructure spending continuing to shoulder much of the growth burden, economists are questioning whether the current surge can be sustained in the coming months.

articles.title: Was Tiger Shroff the real target? | Pulse Maharashtra
articles.summary:
A celebrity shootout in Mumbai has sent shockwaves through the financial capital and has spread fear in the Hindi film industry. This wasn’t the first shootout in the city this year. And now, the industry is scared of the dark shadows of the past, when the underworld called the shots in Bollywood. And just like the past, this time too, the masterminds seem to be operating from foreign shores. But was Tiger Shroff the real target? Is this shootout related to incidents like the firing outside actor Salman Khan’s residence, the murder of NCP leader Baba Siddique, the shooting outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty’s residence and the reported threats to actors Ranveer Singh and Aamir Khan?

In this week’s Pulse Maharashtra with Vinaya Deshpande, we take you through what we know so far and what the unanswered questions are. And how this attack leads to an old fear in the heart of an industry which is one of India’s greatest soft powers in the world – Bollywood.
